build_profile.history: an earlier version of this file recorded a --release flag the run had not used, and the measurement behind it was a debug build. The flag is now true of the run that produced the number.

harness.gate: the test asserts the ratio against a >=1.5x target and prints the raw medians; the gate lives at persistent_hash_indexes in crates/xlog-core/src/config.rs (env XLOG_PERSISTENT_HASH_INDEXES)

limits.dispersion: the harness emits only a median per arm, so this fixture carries no dispersion at all
limits.equivalence: the arms are compared on output row count, not on the row set

same_machine_control.why: the figure this replaces was taken in a debug build, so the run that produced the release number ran both profiles back to back on one pod, one commit, one fixture, to separate the profile from the machine
same_machine_control.reading: release is the HIGHER ratio, which the earlier caveat in this file predicted backwards. The index-rebuilding arm is GPU-bound and barely moves between profiles (15.827 ms debug against 15.784 ms release); the cached arm is host-side and does get faster (2.051 ms against 1.894 ms), so optimizing the build widens the gap instead of closing it.
same_machine_control.host_variation: the debug arm here reads 7.716x against 7.078x from the earlier debug run on a different pod, so roughly 8% of spread is host, not profile
same_machine_control.both_arms_passed: the fixture's own >=1.5x gate passed in both profiles: 'test result: ok. 1 passed' in each log
